tool.description: Start Horizon with the control socket and wait until it answers. Usage: horizon-ctl launch [--world NAME] [--seed N] [--creative] [--version TAG] [--game PATH] [--wait] [GAME ARGS...]. Finds the game in this order: --game PATH; a horizon-client next to horizon-ctl (a build folder, a release folder or a launcher install); the newest version installed by the Horizon launcher (--version TAG picks one). Launcher installs run with their prepared resources and keep saves in the game home ($HORIZON_HOME, else ~/.local/share/horizon). --wait also waits until the player has spawned and chunks are loaded. Other arguments go to the game (horizon-client --help lists them). The game's output goes to a .log file beside the socket.

creative.description: creative mode for a new world

headless.description: no display, window or GPU: a player that plays through these commands only (no screenshots)

offscreen.description: render without showing a window, splitscreen's too (screenshots still work): locked or headless sessions

version.description: an installed launcher version tag such as v2026.10.13

wait.description: also wait until the world is ready (default in MCP)

world.description: world folder to open or create

tool.name: launch

tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): Wait until the game reaches a state, then reply. Usage: horizon-ctl wait-for screen NAME|widget ID|loaded|chat TEXT|event KIND [--timeout S] [--since SEQ]. screen takes the names state shows (playing, inventory, paused, dead, title...); widget an id from ui; loaded means a world is open, the player is in it and no chunk is pending; chat a new line containing TEXT; event a kind from events (death, respawn, item, screen...). chat and event count from --since SEQ (take last from events before acting), else from now. A timeout (default 30 s) is an error with kind timeout.

since.description: chat and event: count from this event seq

value.description: the screen name, widget id, chat text or event kind

tool.name: game_wait_for

tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): What happened since SEQ, oldest first: screens, chat, deaths, respawns, items gained or lost, damage taken (hurt, with its cause), healing, food, dimensions, worlds. Usage: horizon-ctl events [--since SEQ] [--limit N]. Every event has seq and tick; pass the reply's last as --since next time. --limit keeps the newest N and skipped counts the older ones left out. hurt and death carry the player position (a death drops the inventory there). The game keeps the newest 256.
tool.name: game_events

tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): Recent input and who caused it: a person, an agent or the game. Usage: horizon-ctl input-log [--since SEQ] [--limit N] [--origin user|agent|game]. Every event has seq, tick and origin. `user` is the window's own keyboard, mouse or pad; `agent` is the control socket (this tool); `game` is input the game made up. A `user-input` event in `events` means a person stepped in while an agent was driving. The game keeps the newest 512.
tool.name: game_input_log

tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): Wait until the player has spawned and no chunks are pending. Usage: horizon-ctl wait-ready [SECONDS]. Polls status every 250 ms; replies with the status, or an error after SECONDS (default 120).
tool.name: game_wait_ready

tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): The end of the game's log, or its newest crash report. Usage: horizon-ctl logs [--lines N] [--crash]. Reads the game home ($HORIZON_HOME, else ~/.local/share/horizon): logs/latest.log (the last N lines, default 100) or, with --crash, the newest file in crash-reports. Read-only; works whether the game runs or not.
tool.name: game_logs

tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): Game, renderer and streaming state (the scripting socket's original summary). Usage: horizon-ctl status. Also what F3 shows: the overlay flags, the renderer, chunk streaming and memory.
tool.name: game_status

day_time.description: the world's time of day, ticks

debug.description: the F3 overlay flags: overlay, hitboxes, chunk_borders, pause_menu, advanced_tooltips, pause_on_lost_focus, clipboard

dimension.description: the dimension the player is in

held.description: the held stack as item and count; null when empty

keys.description: the keys the game holds down, each a string

lod.description: far terrain: distances, tiles, quads and sampling progress

offhand.description: the offhand stack as item, count and damage; null when empty

pending_chunks.description: chunks still being generated, meshed, uploaded or received

player.description: position, velocity (blocks), on_ground, health, max_health, food; null without a player

renderer.description: GPU, driver, backend, size, draw counts and GPU memory; null without a renderer

server.description: the connected server's address, name and state; null when not connected

streaming.description: chunk streaming stages and their counts

target.description: the block under the crosshair as pos and block; null when none

Replies protocol (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH of the control protocol, docs/api/stability.md), release (the game's version, the string MCP serverInfo carries too) and features (the command groups the game answers, so a script can test for one before calling it).
tool.name: game_hello

features.description: the command groups the game answers, each a string

release.description: the game's version (MCP serverInfo carries the same string)

tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): What holds the game's memory: resident set, allocator, client and server columns by part, renderer, GPU memory by resource. Usage: horizon-ctl memory. Columns count blocks, biomes, light, heightmaps and records, each shared section once; server_columns are the single-player server thread's own levels. GPU memory by label needs Vulkan or DirectX 12. What the census doesn't reach is the resident set less its parts. A build with the alloc-census feature adds heap_by_tag_mb: the live heap by startup step, timed span, chunk job and thread.
tool.name: game_memory

tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): Walk in a direction relative to the view for a time. Usage: horizon-ctl move forward|back|left|right SECONDS [--sprint] [--sneak] [--jump]. Replies when done with the start and end positions.

tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): Walk to a position, finding a path through loaded terrain. Usage: horizon-ctl goto X Y Z [--near R] [--sprint] [--direct] [--timeout S]. A* over standable blocks (steps up one block, drops up to three, avoids lava, swims when it must), then steering with jumps when stuck. Whole-number X and Z name a block and aim at its center (8 64 3 is 8.5 64 3.5); decimals are exact positions. Without a path it fails at once (--direct walks straight at the target anyway, falls included). --near R stops within R blocks (use 1.5-3 to reach a block you then break). Replies with arrived, position and distance, or an error when stuck or out of time (default 60 s).

direct.description: walk straight when no path is found

timeout.description: give up after this many seconds (default 60)

tool.name: game_goto

tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): Jump once and reply when landed. Usage: horizon-ctl jump
tool.name: game_jump

tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): Set the view direction in degrees. Usage: horizon-ctl look YAW PITCH. Yaw 0 faces south (+Z), 90 west (-X), 180 north, -90 east; pitch 90 looks straight down.
tool.name: game_look

tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): Rotate the view by an amount. Usage: horizon-ctl turn DYAW DPITCH [--over S]. Without --over the view jumps. tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): Move the mouse: relative motion that turns the view like a player's mouse. Usage: horizon-ctl mouse-move DX DY. DX and DY are mouse units (pixels of relative motion) added to the frame's accumulated movement and turned by MouseHandler.turnPlayer: degrees = units x 0.15 x (sensitivity x 0.6 + 0.2)^3 x 8 (without the 8 while scoping), inverted axes and the cinematic camera included. tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): Reset frame stats, wait, reply with the summary. Usage: horizon-ctl bench SECONDS [raw]. tool.name: game_stats

tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): Capture the game's performance to a .hzperf file in reports/ in the game home. Usage: horizon-ctl profile [client|server] start [--seconds S] [--hz N] [--over MS] [--threads main|all] [--wall] [--gpu[=detail]] [--no-samples] [--timeline] | stop [--bench REPORT] | status | mark NAME | open FILE | share FILE. start records the frame times, the health history and the render thread's call trees until stop or --seconds (at most 600). stop replies with the file's path once the file is whole, and with the viewer's address (open_at) only in a build that has a part to open captures; open FILE serves the file once on 127.0.0.1 and opens the viewer on it, share FILE uploads it and replies with the link; both fail in a build without that part and work with every telemetry switch off; status says whether a capture runs, its age and its size; mark NAME puts a label at the current time. F3+O does start and stop from the keyboard; HORIZON_PROFILE=DIR records the first 10 minutes of a run into DIR. --gpu adds each render pass's median GPU time and --gpu=detail the dispatch times and, on Vulkan, fragment and vertex counts per pass; HORIZON_SHADER_PACK_TIMING and HORIZON_GPU_PASS_DETAIL start a capture with them. stop --bench REPORT embeds a benchmark report (benchmarks/*.json) in the capture; --benchmark --profile does this by itself. Read the file with horizon-perf (query gpu). With no side a single-player run captures both sides in one file (the window, and the server thread as its own section); client or server captures one. Connected to a Horizon server, server asks that server to capture its side: it needs operator level 4, only one server capture runs at a time, and the server keeps the file in its reports/ and logs who asked; a refusal is a warning in the window's own capture.

bench.description: stop: the path of a benchmark report to embed in the capture

gpu.description: start: also record each render pass's GPU time (detail: its parts and counters too)

name.description: mark: the label; open and share: the file

no-samples.description: start: record frame times and health only

over.description: start: sample only frames slower than this many milliseconds

seconds.description: start: stop after this many seconds, 1 to 600

side.description: client or server, for the window or the server (the single-player server thread, or the server joined); both when omitted

threads.description: start: the render thread (default) or every thread that opted in

timeline.description: start: also record every thread's spans, for 60 seconds at most

wall.description: start: also sample on the wall clock, to find waits

tool.name: game_profile

tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): Record input, state and the world for a bug repro. Usage: horizon-ctl record-start [NAME] [--no-world]. Writes recordings/<stamp>-NAME/: inputs.jsonl (who caused each input: user, agent or game), state.jsonl (the player and world every second), events.jsonl and, in single player, a copy of the world. The recording starts from a fresh save. Replies once the world copy is done.

name.description: folder name after the timestamp (default session)

no-world.description: do not copy the world (a server session)

tool.name: game_record_start

tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): Stop the recording (and write the repro zip). Usage: horizon-ctl record-stop [--export]. Without --export only the recording folder is closed; repro-export zips it later. With --export the reply carries the zip path.

tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): The running recording and replay, if any. Usage: horizon-ctl record-status
tool.name: game_record_status

tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): The recordings and repro bundles on disk. Usage: horizon-ctl record-list
tool.name: game_record_list

tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): Replay a recording, best effort. Usage: horizon-ctl record-replay NAME [--stop] [--in-place] [--keep-world] [--timeout S]. Loads the recording's world copy into saves/, opens it and feeds the recorded input back at its ticks. Only input and movement commands replay (never world, network or account ones). --in-place feeds the input into the world already open (a server recording needs it); --keep-world leaves the copied world behind when it ends. --stop ends a running replay. Same build and machine only; state.jsonl is the oracle, not a promise.

in-place.description: feed the open world instead of opening the copy

keep-world.description: leave the copied world in saves/

timeout.description: give up after this many seconds (default 300)

tool.name: game_record_replay

tool.description: In the running game (start it with play): Zip a recording with the logs, crash report and status. Usage: horizon-ctl repro-export [NAME] [PATH] [--no-world]. Writes repro/<stamp>-NAME.zip: the recording, logs/latest.log, the newest crash report, a status.json and a README. The player attaches it to the bug report; nothing is uploaded. Stops a running recording first.
tool.name: game_repro_export
